name: Skull Rock
summary: Margoz sends you into Skull Rock, east of Orgrimmar. Burning Blade cultists have overrun the cave and use painful demonic devices to bind themselves to dark magic. Margoz needs the cursed artifacts to study the cult's presence near the capital.

sections.title: A Den of Shadows
sections.body: In northeastern Durotar, cultists gather close to Orgrimmar's gates. The cave lies among the hills, far from the open roads, yet near the Warchief's seat. The Burning Blade, a demonic cult that has long plagued orcish society, has made its home in the tunnels. Its followers perform rituals there while the Warchief's scouts watch nearby.

sections.title: Demonic Attunement
sections.body: Burning Blade cultists wear Searing Collars around their necks, metal bands that scorch and brand their flesh. Margoz believes the pain and fel sorcery in the collars attune their wearers to demonic power. He asks you to recover the collars so he can study the spells and bindings that empower the cultists.

sections.title: The Looming Threat
sections.body: The Burning Blade's Searing Collars show that the cult is organized in Durotar. Its sorcery threatens the Horde's newly established territories. Margoz's study of the collars leads to further inquiries among the hidden circles of Orgrimmar.

faq.answer: Skull Rock lies in northeastern Durotar, east of Orgrimmar and north of Sen'jin Village. Its entrance is framed by a craggy cliffside along the shore.

The Burning Blade is a cult of orcs and fel-worshipers devoted to demons and dark magic. Though the modern Horde broke from demonic servitude, splinter groups like the Burning Blade still practice forbidden rites and seek to corrupt the Horde from the shadows.

faq.q: What do the cultists use the Searing Collars for?
faq.answer: Cultists wear Searing Collars around their necks, where the fiery metal burns their flesh. Margoz suspects the pain and demonic enchantment help them channel and attune themselves to dark fel energies.
Margoz is an orcish hermit who lives in a small camp atop the bluffs of Durotar, near Skull Rock. He watches cultist movements along the coast and works to dismantle the Burning Blade's operations.

faq.q: Why does the Horde allow the cult so close to Orgrimmar?
aliases: why is skull rock near orgrimmar
faq.answer: The Horde does not knowingly tolerate the cult near Orgrimmar. Burning Blade followers hide in caves and desolate ravines beyond the reach of regular patrols, and adventurers investigate when the cult's rituals reveal its footholds.

faq.q: What happens after Margoz examines the collars?
faq.answer: Margoz plans to examine the Searing Collars. His investigation continues with Neeru Fireblade in Orgrimmar.

angles.text: As an orc, you face the Burning Blade as a remnant of the dark past your people fight to leave behind. Driving the cult from Durotar's rocks is a matter of survival and honor.
As a warlock, you can see how the Searing Collars bind their wearers with fel magic. Their crude enchantments show how the cult turns demonic sacrifice into power.
As a member of the Horde, you face a demonic cult entrenched just beyond Orgrimmar's walls, threatening the heart and security of your people.
